content.text:
Here's the revised plan, combining ENG-2263 and ENG-2266 on this branch, built fresh from `main`.

## What `main` does today

- All three popovers (type filter, sort, display options) use the same component, [SearchDropdown.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/SearchDropdown.tsx). They only appear in the search modal's toolbar, so changing the shared component affects only these three.
- **Only one popover is open at a time.** The modal tracks which one is open, and clicking another trigger already switches to it ([NodeSearchModal.tsx:535](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx:535)). Your first point needs no new code, as long as the click-blocking below makes an exception for triggers.
- **Outside clicks** close the popover, but the click still goes through, so clicking a result while the sort menu is open also selects it.
- **Tab** isn't handled. It moves through the popover and on into the rest of the modal, and the popover stays open.
- **Opening a popover never moves focus into it**, and none of them respond to arrow keys.
- **The premature-close bug in ENG-2263 never happens on `main`.** It came from closing the popover when focus left it. I'll handle Tab as a key press instead, so that bug can't come back, and the live check will confirm label clicks work.

## Changes

**`SearchDropdown.tsx`: behaviour for all three popovers**
1. **Focus on open.** Focus moves to the selected option if the panel has one (the sort menu's current choice). Otherwise it goes to the first item: the type search box or first checkbox, or the display toggle.
2. **Arrow keys.** ArrowUp and ArrowDown move through the panel's focusable items in on-screen order, wrapping at both ends. The panel's items are looked up when the key is pressed, so the three menus don't each need their own refs. For the sort menu, that's the five rows, then Asc and Desc.
3. **Tab and Shift+Tab** close the popover and put focus back on its trigger. They do nothing else.
4. **Outside click** closes the popover and blocks that click, so whatever was under the pointer doesn't react. **The exception** is another popover's trigger: that click goes through and opens that popover. The triggers get a data attribute so they can be recognised.
5. **Escape** behaves as today: it closes the popover and returns focus to the search input.

**The three menus: focus ring only.** Sort rows, the Asc/Desc buttons and the display toggle are `div`s, so each gets an inset ring on `:focus-visible`, in Obsidian's focus colour. The ring is drawn with a `[box-shadow:…]` arbitrary value because Tailwind's `ring-*` classes don't work in this plugin. The type filter's native checkboxes and search box keep Obsidian's own ring. No other markup changes.

## Verification

- **Static checks:** `tsc` and `eslint` on the changed files, with zero warnings, since CI fails on lint warnings on added lines.
- **Live check** in Obsidian on dgDevVault, run with `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify` and checking each popover:
  - **Opening:** opening with Enter on the trigger puts focus inside, and the ring shows. Opening with the mouse shows no ring.
  - **Arrow keys:** they visit every item and wrap at both ends, for example 7 stops in the sort menu.
  - **Tab and Shift+Tab:** the popover closes, focus lands on its trigger, and nothing else changes.
  - **Clicking outside:** clicking a result or the search box only closes the popover. The active result and the selection don't change.
  - **Switching:** with sort open, clicking the filter trigger closes sort and opens the filter in one click.
  - **Type filter labels:** clicking a row's label text or colour dot toggles it every time, which covers ENG-2263's second Done When item.
  - **Escape:** closes the popover and returns focus to the search input.
  - **Results:** arrow keys while a popover is open never move the highlighted result.
  - **Screenshots:** the ring in each popover, in light and dark themes, attached to the PR.

## Tickets and John: nothing sent until you say so

- **Linear:** I'd update ENG-2266 so its Done When covers the combined behaviour, and mark ENG-2263 as a duplicate of it. Shall I draft both edits for you to review first?
- **Message to John:** I'll draft a short note for you to send, saying the combined change replaces his drafts #1446 and #1451.

Do you want any changes to the plan, or should I start on `SearchDropdown.tsx`?

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```

➡️ <your recommended answer>

Word each question so "yes" accepts your recommended answer.

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

content.text:
I mapped the design tree from the agreed plan. Already settled: ENG-2263 and ENG-2266 are combined, the work starts fresh from `main`, clicking another popover's trigger switches to it, and Tab returns focus to the trigger. Here is round 1, the questions that don't depend on each other.

❓ **Q1 - Escape keeps its current focus target**: Today Escape closes the popover and focuses the search input. Tab now returns focus to the trigger, so the two keys would land in different places. Options:
- (a) Leave Escape as is, since Escape means "back to searching".
- (b) Make Escape return to the trigger too, so all closes behave the same.

➡️ (a) Leave Escape as is. Escape-to-input is existing, shipped behaviour, and changing it is outside both tickets.

---

❓ **Q2 - Every click outside the panel only closes it, including outside the modal**: Besides other triggers, an outside click can land on:
- the search input
- a result
- the preview pane
- the footer buttons
- the modal's close ✕
- the dimmed background behind the modal, which normally closes the whole modal

Should every one of these only close the popover?

➡️ Yes, all of them. A click on the dimmed background or the ✕ closes the popover but leaves the modal open. A second click is needed to close the modal.

---

❓ **Q3 - Hovering a result while a popover is open leaves the highlight alone**: Results take the highlight when the pointer moves over them ([NodeSearchModal.tsx:306-316](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx:306)). The sort menu hangs over the results list, so moving to an option drags the pointer across results and moves the highlight. Hover isn't a click, but it is an "other action".

➡️ Yes, ignore result hover while any popover is open. The highlight stays where it was when the popover opened.

---

❓ **Q4 - Clicking the open popover's own trigger still closes it**: Today the trigger toggles. Keep that?

➡️ Yes, keep the toggle.

---

❓ **Q5 - Selecting an option leaves the popover open**: Today choosing a sort option, ticking a filter or flipping the display toggle keeps the panel open. Should it stay that way, including when you press Enter or Space on a sort row?

➡️ Yes, stay open. Filters and sort are often adjusted together (for example, a key and then its direction), and Escape or Tab closes the panel in one key.

---

❓ **Q6 - In the type filter, ArrowUp from the first checkbox wraps to the last item**: When there are many types, the filter panel has a search box above the checkboxes. Options:
- (a) The search box is just another item in the wrapping list: ArrowUp from the first checkbox goes to the search box, and ArrowUp from the search box goes to the last checkbox.
- (b) As in ENG-2263: the search box is outside the loop, ArrowUp from the first checkbox goes to the search box, and ArrowDown from the last checkbox wraps to the first checkbox.

➡️ (a) The search box is part of the loop. That way one generic rule covers all three popovers with no special case. Note that a "yes" here means (a), even though the title above describes neither option exactly.

---

❓ **Q7 - Enter toggles a type filter checkbox**: Native checkboxes respond to Space but ignore Enter. Sort rows and the display toggle accept both keys. Should Enter also toggle a checkbox?

➡️ Yes. One rule for the popovers: Enter and Space both activate the focused item.

---

❓ **Q8 - Home/End, ArrowLeft/Right and type-to-jump stay out of scope**: These are common menu extras:
- Home/End jump to the first or last item.
- Left/Right switch between Asc and Desc.
- Typing a letter jumps to the next item starting with it.

None of them is in either ticket's Done When.

➡️ Yes, out of scope. I'd mention them as follow-ups in the PR.

---

❓ **Q9 - The menus' ARIA roles stay as they are**: Rows use `menuitemradio` and `menuitemcheckbox`, but the panel has no `role="menu"`, and the type filter panel has plain checkboxes. Fixing that properly means a role change in all three menus and screen-reader testing.

➡️ Yes, leave the ARIA roles as they are. This PR is about keyboard behaviour, and I'd file an accessibility follow-up ticket if you want one.

---

❓ **Q10 - The arrow-key wrap logic goes in a small pure helper with a Vitest test**: The wrap logic is "given the items and the focused one, which is next". It could stay inline in `SearchDropdown`, which is only tested live. Or it could be a pure function in `src/utils` with a unit test, matching the convention of committing tests for new helpers.

➡️ Yes, use a pure helper plus a Vitest test, because the wrap rules are where off-by-one bugs live.

---

❓ **Q11 - Rename ENG-2266 to cover the merged scope**: Its current title is about the sort menu only, and the PR title has to match the ticket title exactly. A suggested title is "Make advanced node search popovers keyboard controllable". I'd also rewrite its Done When to the combined list and mark ENG-2263 as a duplicate. I'd draft all of that for your review before anything goes to Linear.

➡️ Yes, rename it and draft the Linear edits for your approval.

---

❓ **Q12 - Tell John with a short note that I draft and you send**: His drafts #1446 and #1451 would be replaced. Options:
- (a) I draft a Slack or DM note for you to send.
- (b) I draft a comment on #1446 and #1451 for you to approve, then post it.
- (c) You handle it yourself.

➡️ (a) I draft a short note for you to send, and his drafts stay untouched.

content.text:
Answers to your three questions first:

**Q2: your split matches how established menus behave.** There are two common conventions:
- **Menus that block the page.** Radix and macOS native menus, and Linear's menus, swallow the outside click: it only dismisses the menu.
- **Popovers that let clicks through.** Headless UI's popovers and most "filter" panels close and also let the click act.

What you describe is the usual middle ground. Clicks whose intent is unmistakable go through: the search box, the modal's ✕, and another popover's trigger. Everything else, such as a result or the preview, only closes the popover. A stray click on a result that opens a file would be a nasty surprise, while closing the modal is clearly deliberate. That gives these answers:
- The ✕ closes the popover and the modal in one click.
- A click on the search box closes the popover and places the caret where you clicked.
- Results and the preview only close the popover.

That raises a few edge cases, which are in round 2 below.

**Q3: "highlight" means the active result.** It's the row Enter would open, and the one shown in the preview pane. Hovering over a result moves that highlight, and the preview follows. Keyboard focus is a separate thing: hover never takes it, so focus stays in the popover whatever the mouse does. So yes, the mouse can keep doing what it does today with no code change. The only visible effect is that sweeping the pointer across the results on the way to the menu changes the highlight and the preview. That's harmless and arguably expected, so I'll drop my recommendation and leave hover alone.

**Q6: yes, it's simpler.** With the search box in the loop, one rule covers all three popovers: "every focusable item in the panel, in on-screen order; arrow keys step and wrap." Keeping the search box outside the loop, as ENG-2263 did, means the shared component needs a special case for "the text box at the top". The only cost is that ArrowUp/ArrowDown in that one-line box won't jump the caret to the start or end, which nobody relies on. Left/Right still move the caret.

**Settled from your answers:**
- Q7: no Enter handling on the filter checkboxes.
- Q10: no Vitest; the wrap logic stays inline and the live test carries the weight.
- Q1, Q4, Q5, Q8, Q9, Q11 and Q12 are accepted as I recommended.

Round 2 covers the edge cases your Q2 split creates:

❓ **Q13 - Clicking the dimmed background only closes the popover**: The dimmed area behind the modal normally closes the whole modal. It's less deliberate than the ✕, since it's easy to hit when you overshoot a panel near the edge.

➡️ Yes, it only closes the popover, and the modal stays open.

---

❓ **Q14 - The footer's "esc close" button goes through like the ✕**: The footer has a clickable "esc close" hint that closes the modal, so it means the same as the ✕.

➡️ Yes, treat it like the ✕: one click closes both the popover and the modal.

---

❓ **Q15 - The footer's action buttons only close the popover**: "Insert link", "Open in new tab" and "Open in split" act on the highlighted result, which is the same risk as clicking a result.

➡️ Yes, they're blocked: the click only closes the popover.

---

❓ **Q16 - Type chips inside the search box count as the search box**: The search box holds type chips. Each chip can be clicked to focus it and has a small × to remove its filter. Options:
- (a) Clicks on the chips go through like the rest of the search box.
- (b) Only the text area goes through, and chip clicks only close the popover.

➡️ (a) They go through. The chips are part of the search box, the user is clearly aiming at them, and removing a chip is easy to undo.

---

❓ **Q17 - Clicks that go through are marked by the modal, not looked up by shape**: The shared popover needs to know which clicks may go through. Options:
- (a) Mark those elements with a data attribute, such as `data-popover-passthrough`: the triggers, the search box wrapper, the ✕ and the "esc close" button.
- (b) Detect them inside the popover with selectors like `.modal-close-button`.

➡️ (a) A data attribute. The rule is visible where each element is defined, and the shared component doesn't need to know the modal's layout. The ✕ belongs to Obsidian, not React, so the code sets the attribute on it once when the modal opens.

content.text:
I checked one fact that simplifies things a lot: **a single click on a result doesn't open it.** It only moves the highlight, the same as hovering ([NodeSearchModal.tsx:317](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSearchModal.tsx:317)). Opening needs Enter or a footer button. So no click outside a popover can do anything accidental:

| Click target | Effect |
|---|---|
| Result | Moves the highlight only |
| Search box | Focuses it |
| ✕, "esc close", footer buttons | Intentional actions (you said so for the footer in Q15) |
| Another trigger | Opens that popover |

That means every exception we were designing is protecting against nothing.

## Simplest option (recommended): standard light-dismiss, no exceptions

"Light dismiss" is the default behaviour of a popover that doesn't block the page: an outside click closes it and the click still does its normal job. Headless UI, the browser's own popover feature, and most filter panels work this way, and **it's what `main` already does**. The whole design comes down to six rules:

1. **One popover at a time.** Already on `main`.
2. **Opening moves focus inside.** It goes to the selected option, or else the first item. New.
3. **ArrowUp/ArrowDown step through every focusable item in the panel and wrap.** The search box is part of the loop. New.
4. **Tab/Shift+Tab close the popover and return focus to its trigger.** New, and this is the one place we hold the action back, as you asked.
5. **Escape closes it and focuses the search box.** Already on `main`.
6. **An outside click closes it, and the click goes through.** Already on `main`. Q13–Q17 go away, there are no data attributes, and the ✕ gets no special handling.

All of it lives in `SearchDropdown.tsx`, plus a focus-ring class on the `div` items in the sort and display menus.

The only gap against your original point 3: clicking something like the dimmed background, or a link in the preview, does its normal job after closing the popover. All of those are deliberate clicks, so I think that's correct.

## A very different idea: Obsidian's native `Menu` for sort and display options

Obsidian's own menu (the one behind right-click menus, and already used in [helpMenu.ts](apps/obsidian/src/utils/helpMenu.ts)) supports checkmarks (`setChecked`), sections and positioning. It handles one-at-a-time, outside clicks, Escape and styling itself, and probably arrow keys too, though I haven't verified that.
- **For:** almost no custom code for those two menus, and it looks native, in line with your "Obsidian-native components first" preference.
- **Against:**
  - Obsidian's menus close after each pick, so choosing a key and then a direction takes two opens.
  - It's a visual redesign of menus that are already shipped.
  - The type filter can't use it, because of its search box and multi-select, so we'd end up running two popover systems.

**I'd skip it** for this ticket. It could make sense as a follow-up idea if the plugin later goes all-native.

I also rejected the browser's built-in popover feature. It would give one-at-a-time and outside-click handling for free, but it renders the panel in a separate top layer, so it would lose its position under its trigger. It could also fight Obsidian over Escape.

---

❓ **Q18 - Use standard light dismiss: an outside click closes the popover and the click still does its normal job, with no exceptions**: This replaces the pass-through list from Q2 and Q13–Q17. Tab still only closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger.

➡️ Yes. It's the standard behaviour, mostly already built, and no outside click on this modal is destructive.

We've settled everything, so here's the full spec for you to confirm before I write any code.

## ENG-2266: keyboard control for the search popovers

The ENG-2263 work is folded in, built fresh from `main`, and John's drafts stay untouched. The rules apply to all three toolbar popovers: type filter, sort and display options.

| # | Rule | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | One popover open at a time. Clicking another trigger switches to it. Clicking the open popover's own trigger closes it. | Already on `main` |
| 2 | Opening moves focus inside: to the selected option if there is one (sort), otherwise the first item (the type search box or first checkbox, or the display toggle). | New |
| 3 | ArrowUp/ArrowDown step through every focusable item in the panel, in on-screen order, and wrap at both ends. The type search box is part of the loop. | New |
| 4 | Tab and Shift+Tab only close the popover and return focus to its trigger. | New |
| 5 | Escape closes it and focuses the search box. | Already on `main` |
| 6 | An outside click closes it, and the click does its normal job. | Already on `main` |
| 7 | Choosing an option leaves the popover open. | Already on `main` |
| 8 | A keyboard-only focus ring (`:focus-visible`) on the `div` items: sort rows, Asc/Desc, the display toggle. Native checkboxes and inputs keep Obsidian's ring. | New |

**Where it lives:** `SearchDropdown.tsx` for rules 2–4, plus the ring class in `NodeSortMenu.tsx` and `NodeDisplayOptionsMenu.tsx`. The arrow-key logic stays inline, with no helper or Vitest test.

**Not changing:**
- The filter checkboxes stay as they are (no Enter toggle).
- Hovering results still moves the highlight.
- ARIA roles stay as they are.
- Out of scope: Home/End, Left/Right and type-to-jump. I'll list them as follow-ups in the PR.

**Verification:** `tsc` and `eslint` with zero warnings, then a live check in Obsidian on dgDevVault, run with `dg-obsidian-cdp-verify`:
- Rules 1–8 on each popover.
- In the type filter, clicking a label or colour dot toggles the row every time (ENG-2263's Done When).
- Arrow keys inside a popover never move the highlighted result.
- Screenshots of the ring in light and dark themes.

**Linear and John:** nothing is sent until you approve it. I'll draft the ENG-2266 rename ("Make advanced node search popovers keyboard controllable"), its new Done When, the "duplicate" link from ENG-2263, and a short note for you to send John.

Does this match your understanding? If so, I'll start implementing and put the Linear drafts in front of you alongside.

content.content: @AGENTS.md

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify

# Obsidian CDP verify

## The one command

From the worktree root:

```sh
node ~/.claude/skills/dg-obsidian-cdp-verify/scripts/run.mjs \
  --marker "<string only this change's bundle contains>" \
  --scenario path/to/scenarios.mjs [--scenario more.mjs] [--port 9222] [--skip-build]
```

It runs claim → doctor → launch → deliver → scenarios → cleanup and prints the `last-run.json` path, the scenario matrix, and the `pr-evidence` args. Exit codes: 0 all pass, 1 failure, 2 no vault available or vault locked, 3 marker missing.

On exit 2 with `candidates`, follow the `obsidian-vault` skill: ask Trang which vault to take, then run `vault.mjs claim --take` and rerun.

Write scenario files in the session scratchpad, not the repo.

## Launch

- With no `--slot`, the vault is this worktree's `obsidian-vault` lease. `run.mjs` claims a free one if the worktree has no lease yet. This keeps the CDP run in the vault the worktree's watcher builds into.
- `--slot N` is a legacy override. It's a 1-based index into `OBSIDIAN_VERIFY_VAULTS` in `<worktree>/apps/obsidian/.env` and bypasses leases, so use it only when Trang names a slot.
- If Obsidian is running on the debug port, the script attaches.
- If it's running without the port, the script quits Obsidian and relaunches it with `--remote-debugging-port`. Trang approved this; the windows come back.
- If it isn't running, the script launches it with the port.
- It then opens the slot vault through `obsidian://open?path=` and waits for a page target where `.workspace` exists and `app.vault.adapter.basePath` matches the vault.
- It writes the lock `<vault>/.obsidian/dg-verify.lock` (`{pid, branch, startedAt}`) and releases it in `finally`.

## Doctor

`scripts/doctor.mjs [--slot N]` is read-only and prints JSON: the resolved vault, the lock and the Obsidian state. It exits 2 if the worktree has no lease, or if another live run holds the lock. A lock left by a dead pid is ignored.

## Deliver

`scripts/deliver.mjs --marker <str>` also runs on its own.

1. `OBSIDIAN_PLUGIN_PATH=<slot plugin dir> tsx scripts/build.ts` runs once in `apps/obsidian`. It also writes `apps/obsidian/dist`, which is gitignored.
2. It greps the vault's `main.js` for `--marker` and fails if the marker is absent.
3. It reloads the plugin. The plugin id and folder are resolved from the manifests.
4. It greps again.
5. It warns about other worktrees' apps/obsidian `dev.ts` watchers that mirror into this vault. Your own worktree's watcher builds the same code, so it isn't flagged.

The harness also hashes `main.js` before and after the scenarios. If it changed, the run is marked invalid.

## Drive: scenario contract

A module's `export default` is one scenario or an array of them:

```js
export default {
  name: "Search modal renders",                 // matrix row + screenshot name
  input: "run open-node-search",                // matrix text
  expected: "modal with a textbox and footer",  // matrix text
  setup: async (ctx) => ({ /* state; snapshot anything you change */ }),  // optional
  run: async ({ client, json, vault }, state) => {
    await client.evaluate(`return app.commands.executeCommandById(${json(`${vault.pluginId}:open-node-search`)});`);
    await client.waitFor(`!!document.querySelector(".dg-node-search-modal [role=textbox]")`);
    return client.evaluate(`document.querySelectorAll(".dg-search-footer-action").length`);
  },
  expect: (actual, state) => ({ pass: actual > 0, actual: `${actual} footer actions` }),  // or a boolean
  teardown: async (ctx, state) => {},           // optional: restore what setup changed
};
```

- `ctx` has `client`, `vault` (`root`, `pluginId`, `pluginDir`), `branch`, `json`, `verifyPath(name)` and `writeNote(name, body)`. `writeNote` creates or overwrites `_verify/<branch>/<name>` and returns its path.
- `client` has `evaluate`, `waitFor`, `key`, `typeText`, `pressEscape`, `screenshot`, `reloadPlugin`, `clearModals` and `send` (raw CDP).
- The harness does these for you:
  - Before each scenario, it clears modals and restores the layout captured at the start of the run.
  - After `run`, it takes a screenshot.
  - A thrown error becomes a failing row.
- The worked example is `examples/insert-link-at-cursor.mjs` (ENG-2114, 3 scenarios).

## Evidence

- The artifacts go to `<worktree>/local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/<branch>/<runStamp>/`: `<n>-<slug>.png` and `last-run.json` (`results[]` of `{scenario, input, expected, actual, pass, screenshot}`).
- Paste the printed matrix into create-pr's Evidence section.
- Upload the screenshots with pr-evidence, using the printed args:

```sh
./apps/roam/node_modules/.bin/tsx ~/.claude/skills/pr-evidence/upload.ts --harness obsidian-cdp <printed args>
```

## Cleanup

- Cleanup dismisses modals (Escape, then force-removes leftover `.modal-container`), restores the baseline layout and releases the lock.
- **It never deletes folders or notes.** `_verify/<branch>/` persists, and reruns overwrite its notes.
- Scenarios that change vault or app settings must restore them in `teardown`.

## Gotchas

These are the ones the code can't handle for you.

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
| --- | --- |
| Double-handled keypress | Pass `type` to `client.key` only through its loop. Never send your own `keyDown`. |
| `editor.hasFocus()` false while focus looks right | This can't be measured over CDP. Assert the consequence instead, e.g. the cursor moved past the inserted text. |
| File content assertion fails, editor looks right | Saves are debounced (about 2s). `waitFor` on `app.vault.read(...)`, and don't read once. |
| `getLeaf(true)` throws "No tab group found" | Every markdown leaf was detached. Use `getLeaf("tab")`. |
| Top-level `await` throws in `evaluate` | Bodies run in a plain function. Return an async IIFE or a promise chain. |
| `iterateRootLeaves` count caps at 2 | A truthy callback return stops the iteration. Use a block body `{ n++; }`. |
| Escape handler in a modal child never wins | Obsidian's modal scope runs first. Push a `Scope` with `app.keymap.pushScope`. |
| Styling CodeMirror spans disappears on focus or scroll | Use a CM6 decoration, not MutationObserver stamping. A widget's `ignoreEvent()` must stay `true` for clicks. |
| Selectors from an old ENG example don't match | The UI drifts. The node search input is now a contenteditable `[role=textbox]`, not an `<input>`. |
| Flaky failure that looks like a code bug | Trang may be using the app mid-run. Rerun before believing a single observation. |
| Timers stall, writes land minutes late | Focus emulation normally prevents this. If it recurs, check `document.visibilityState` and ask Trang to show the window. |
| zsh eats `${VAR}` in `node -e` | Write scenarios to `.mjs` files. |
| `waitFor` on an IIFE always times out | `evaluate` adds an outer `return` only when the code contains no `return`. An IIFE with an inner `return` evaluates to `undefined`, so write `return (() => { ... })()`. |
| A note written in `setup` is randomly missing from search results | Datacore indexes new files after the metadata cache, and the search loads through Datacore. After `writeNote`, also `waitFor` `dc.query("@page and exists(nodeTypeId)")` to include the path. |

content.text:
Keyboard control now works in all three search popovers. All 11 live scenarios in Obsidian (dgDevVault) passed on two runs in a row, and lint is clean. The type-check only shows two `gray-matter` errors in test files, which fail the same way on `main`. Nothing is committed yet.

The change is 87 added and 13 removed lines across [SearchDropdown.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/SearchDropdown.tsx), [NodeSortMenu.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeSortMenu.tsx) and [NodeDisplayOptionsMenu.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/NodeDisplayOptionsMenu.tsx). Most of it is in `SearchDropdown.tsx`; the two menus only get the focus-ring class.

**What the live run showed:**
- **Sort menu:** focus starts on the selected row with the ring. ArrowDown goes Relevance → Alphabetical → Date created → Date modified → Author → Asc → Desc → back to Relevance. ArrowUp from Relevance goes to Desc. The highlighted result never moves.
- **Tab and Shift+Tab:** the popover closes, focus lands on its trigger, and the sort is unchanged.
- **Mouse open:** no ring anywhere. The first ArrowDown rings the first row.
- **Switching:** with sort open, one click on the filter trigger closes sort and opens the filter.
- **Outside click on a result:** the popover closes and that result gets highlighted, so the click still goes through.
- **Escape:** the popover closes and focus returns to the search box. The modal stays open.
- **Type filter:** the arrow keys wrap through every item. Clicking a row's label text or colour dot toggles it every time, which covers ENG-2263's Done When.
- **Display options:** focus lands on the toggle with the ring, and Enter flips it without closing the popover.
- **Dark theme:** the ring is visible.

**One deviation from the plan.** Opening a popover with the mouse puts focus on the panel itself, not on the selected item. Chromium shows the keyboard ring on anything focused straight from the search box, so focusing the item made the ring appear on mouse opens. Keyboard opens still put focus on the selected item.

**Decision for you:** the filter's hidden "Only" buttons are arrow-key stops. Each type row takes two presses, the checkbox and then its "Only" button, which appears when focused (screenshot 8). With 4 types that's 8 stops. Should the arrow keys skip "Only" buttons, leaving them reachable by Tab only? It's a one-line change to which elements the arrows visit, but it's a special case in the shared component, so I left it as is.

**Also worth knowing:**
- The dgDevVault window disappeared once during the first run. The rerun passed with the window still open, so I believe it was closed from outside the run, but I can't prove that.
- The screenshots and `last-run.json` are in `local/obsidian-cdp/artifacts/.../2026-10-17T14-40-44/`, ready to upload to the PR with pr-evidence.

**Drafts for your review (nothing sent):**

*Linear, ENG-2266*, retitled "Make advanced node search popovers keyboard controllable". New Done When:
- Opening a popover by keyboard focuses its selected item, or its first item. Opening it by mouse shows no focus ring.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown move through every item in the popover and wrap at both ends.
- Tab and Shift+Tab only close the popover and return focus to its trigger.
- An outside click closes the popover, and the click still takes effect. Clicking another popover's trigger switches to it.
- Clicking a filter row's label or colour dot toggles it every time.
- The focus ring shows for keyboard navigation only (`:focus-visible`).

Then mark ENG-2263 as a duplicate of ENG-2266.

*Note to John:*
> Hey John, heads up: I'm folding ENG-2263 into ENG-2266 as one "keyboard control for the search popovers" change, built fresh on main. Your #1446 sits on the closed ENG-2181 branch, so it can't land as-is. That means #1446 and #1451 will be superseded. I borrowed your arrow-wrap and focus-on-open ideas. Happy to walk through it, and shout if anything in those drafts should still carry over.

Next: your call on the "Only" stops and your OK on the drafts. Then I'll commit, run `scope-check`, `dg-pr-adherence-check` and `dg-delegated-full-review`, and open the PR. You can run `/checkpoint` at any point to save this session's context.

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.
## Reviewer brief

<!-- Optional. Remove this section when it adds no value.
Include only the fields that help the reviewer:
- Result: The final behavior or outcome.
- Review focus: A decision, risk, or part of the diff that needs careful review.
- Risk or follow-up: Unresolved, unverified, or deferred work that affects approval.
-->

## Verification

<!-- Optional checks and their results. Remove this section when it adds no value. -->

## Loom video

<!-- Include a short Loom video for every PR (any change—UI, backend, refactors, infra, etc.).
This helps reviewers understand intent quickly and catches issues earlier
- Keep it under 2–3 minutes
- Show before/after for bug fixes
- Narrate key design or dev decisions
- Paste the Loom link in the PR body
-->

## Scope check

- [ ] Ran `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`:

<!-- Add either:
- `None` when the final diff stays within Done When.
- What changed, why it is required now, whether anyone was affected or consulted, and links to the use case, ticket, or decision.
-->

## Standards check

- [ ] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.

<!-- Checking the box means the review ran, not that every requirement passed.
Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author
so they can address them. -->

## Local delegated full review

- [ ] Ran a comprehensive review of the entire final diff in a subagent with a fresh context. Use `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.

     - With a type filter active, opening the menu by keyboard puts focus on "Clear filter", because it is the first focusable item.
     - Pressing Enter clears the filter and the button disappears, so focus falls to `document.body` while the panel stays open.
     - After that, arrows and Tab never reach SearchDropdown's key handler. Only Escape still works.

     - `tabIndex={-1}` takes the button out of both Tab order and arrow navigation, and no key replaces it.
     - Before this change, keyboard users could Tab to it. Now selecting a single type takes one checkbox toggle per type.
     - The brief says this is intended, but it is still a loss of a keyboard action.

     - The trigger's `onMouseDown` comment says it "keeps focus in the search input" so arrow and Enter navigation stay live.
     - Opening a menu with the pointer now moves focus to the panel. Typing while a menu is open goes to the panel and is swallowed instead of reaching the search box.
  
  4. **Opening by keyboard only looks for `[aria-checked="true"]`.** `apps/obsidian/src/components/SearchDropdown.tsx:69`
     - The type filter uses native checked inputs, so it never focuses a checked type. It always focuses the first item.
     - The direction toggle's `aria-pressed` state is never looked at either.

     - `onOpenChange(false)` runs the modal's `handleDropdownOpenChange`, which focuses the search input. `triggerRef.focus()` then moves focus to the trigger.

  6. **Tab can trap focus on the trigger.** `apps/obsidian/src/components/SearchDropdown.tsx:80`
     - Tab handling also runs when the trigger itself has focus while the menu is open.
     - In that case Tab and Shift+Tab just refocus the trigger and can't move past it until the user presses Escape.
